title: Intrinsic proper/open alpha vertical equation on module sheaves
statement:
Let $B$ be a commutative ring. For each scheme $X$ [def-pc-scheme], use its small pro-etale site [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site], the constant ring sheaf $\underline B_X$ [def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf], and its category of module sheaves [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. Write $P_f$ for the specified inverse-image functor [def-cbc-strict-constant-tower-operations], $L_j$ for exact open extension [def-cbc-strict-tower-open-extension], and $\alpha(k,r,p,i;h):P_pL_i\to L_kP_r$ for the intrinsic ordinary clopen map [def-cbc-strict-tower-ordinary-proper-open-arrows]. The arrows in the following equations include the specified inverse-image compositors $c^P_{f,g}:P_{gf}\cong P_fP_g$, the unit-preserving open compositors $c^L_{i,j}:L_jL_i\cong L_{ji}$, and the cartesian open comparison $\beta$ [lem-cbc-tower-open-beta-normalization]. Let $k:A\hookrightarrow B_0$, $i:C\hookrightarrow D$, and $j:E\hookrightarrow F$ be quasi-compact open immersions [def-weil-open-immersion] [def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. Let $r_1:A\to C$, $r_2:C\to E$, $p_1:B_0\to D$, $p_2:D\to F$ be proper [def-weil-proper-morphism]. Suppose $p_1k=ir_1$, $p_2i=jr_2$, and hence $(p_2p_1)k=j(r_2r_1)$. For every module sheaf $M$ on $E$, the component equation is
$$\alpha(k,r_1,p_1,i)_{P_{r_2}M}\circ P_{p_1}(\alpha(i,r_2,p_2,j)_M)\circ (c^P_{p_1,p_2})_{L_jM}=L_k((c^P_{r_1,r_2})_M)\circ\alpha(k,r_2r_1,p_2p_1,j)_M.$$
This assertion is on module sheaves only.

proof.text: Restriction along k detects morphisms whose target is L_k N. Transport constant-ring modules faithfully to ModuleCat B-valued pro-etale sheaves using the fixed coefficient equivalence and its pullback/open comparisons. In the adopted source library the unit L_k N -> k_* k^* L_k N is monic (mono_upperStarLowerStarAdjunction_unit_app_openImmersionLowerShriek, Open.LocalVanishing). Naturality of this unit therefore detects equality after restriction. This replaces the image/open-closed proof by the existing extension-by-zero monomorphism.

proof.text: Apply the proved single-square restriction normalization to the first, second and outer squares, preserving the precise open units and inverse-image square compositors.

Precompose the restricted proposed identity by the outer square comparison. The vertical square-comparison pasting equation moves this comparison across the horizontal inverse-image compositor. Naturality of the first square comparison moves the second alpha to its restriction. Use the two single-square normalizations. The middle open unit and its inverse cancel under P_r1. Naturality of the r1,r2 inverse-image compositor moves the remaining inverse bottom unit to the left. The normalization for the outer square and naturality of the top unit identify the result with the right side. Cancel the outer square comparison and apply restriction detection.

theorem singleAlpha_vertical {A C E B₀ D F : Scheme.{u}}
    (k : A ⟶ B₀) (i : C ⟶ D) (j : E ⟶ F)
    (r₁ : A ⟶ C) (r₂ : C ⟶ E) (p₁ : B₀ ⟶ D) (p₂ : D ⟶ F)
    [IsOpenImmersion k] [IsOpenImmersion i] [IsOpenImmersion j]
    [QuasiCompact k] [QuasiCompact i] [QuasiCompact j]
    [IsProper r₁] [IsProper r₂] [IsProper p₁] [IsProper p₂]
    (h₁ : k ≫ p₁ = r₁ ≫ i) (h₂ : i ≫ p₂ = r₂ ≫ j)
    (h : k ≫ (p₁ ≫ p₂) = (r₁ ≫ r₂) ≫ j) :
    ∀ M : Modules B E,
      (moduleGComp B p₁ p₂).hom.app ((moduleJ B j).obj M) ≫
          (modulePullback B p₁).map ((singleAlpha B i r₂ p₂ j h₂).app M) ≫
          (singleAlpha B k r₁ p₁ i h₁).app ((modulePullback B r₂).obj M) =
        (singleAlpha B k (r₁ ≫ r₂) (p₁ ≫ p₂) j h).app M ≫
          (moduleJ B k).map ((moduleGComp B r₁ r₂).hom.app M)
